blocking_components.component: released output predates a recorded input
blocking_components.why: 9 output(s) were last written BEFORE an input this manifest records as consumed. The released bytes were not produced by those inputs, so a faithful replay CANNOT reproduce them and should not be expected to.
blocking_components.evidence_strength: mtime only. A content-identical rewrite of an input moves its mtime without changing what it says, so this can flag a release that is in fact current. It stays blocking because the opposite error - shipping a stale table as replayable - is the one that costs money.

blocking_components.component: in-place enricher outside the collection's plan
blocking_components.why: a script wrote these outputs AFTER the rebuilder and is not in the plan, so the manifest's command list does not reproduce the released columns. The evidence is the enricher's own .bak_ file, not an inference.

blocking_components.component: run date stamped into output rows
blocking_components.why: these columns hold one constant date - the day the build ran - so two faithful runs on two days produce different bytes. Compare with the column excluded, or make the column derive from the SOURCE's date rather than the clock.

blocking_components.component: absolute project root hardcoded in code
